snippet.title: Why Copper Could Limit the AI Race
snippet.description:
One AI server rack can hold over two miles of copper cable, yet AI is only a small slice of the world's copper. Why a new mine takes about 17 years, and why that could limit the AI race.

New Shorts every week.

SOURCES
• S&P Global, copper supply gap study, 8 January 2026 (17 years from discovery to production; a 25% shortfall by 2040 is a forecast): https://press.spglobal.com/2026-01-08-Substantial-Shortfall-in-Copper-Supply-Widens-as-the-Race-for-AI-and-Growing-Defense-Spending-Add-to-Accelerating-Demand,-New-S-P-Global-Study-Finds
• USGS, Mineral Commodity Summaries 2026, Copper: https://pubs.usgs.gov/periodicals/mcs2026/mcs2026-copper.pdf
• IEA, Global Critical Minerals Outlook 2025: https://www.iea.org/reports/global-critical-minerals-outlook-2025/overview-of-outlook-for-key-minerals
• Nvidia GB200 NVL72, about 5,000 copper cables and over 2 miles per rack (Nvidia's figures, as reported by LightCounting): https://www.lightcounting.com/research-note/april-2024-all-eyes-on-nvidia-352
• Copper in electric cars, 83 kg against 23 kg (ICSG 2018, cited in this study): https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0921344920305152
• How porphyry copper deposits form (Nature Reviews Earth & Environment, 2021): https://www.nature.com/articles/s43017-021-00182-8
Figures checked on 5 October 2026.

PHOTO CREDITS (Wikimedia Commons)
Server rack cables: Derrick Coetzee from Berkeley, CA, USA, CC0 · Native copper: Flipin,OG, CC0 · Transformer busbars: Wtshymanski, CC BY-SA 3.0 · Transmission line: Eduardo Sanchez, CC0 · Electric car charging: Julian Herzog (Website), CC BY 4.0 · Copper pipes: Achim Hering, CC BY 3.0 · Chalcopyrite: Didier Descouens, CC BY-SA 3.0 · Chuquicamata mine: Diego Delso, CC BY-SA 4.0 · Bingham Canyon Mine: David Ratledge, CC BY 4.0, and Farragutful, CC BY-SA 4.0

The narration and the schematic are AI-generated; the photos are real.

snippet.title: Lithium Isn't Rare, So Why Do Countries Fight Over It?
snippet.description:
Lithium isn't rare, but about 60% of it is refined in one country. How the lightest metal became a pressure point, and the battery that could walk away from it.

New Shorts every week.

SOURCES
• USGS, Mineral Commodity Summaries 2026, Lithium: https://pubs.usgs.gov/periodicals/mcs2026/mcs2026-lithium.pdf
• IEA, Global Critical Minerals Outlook 2025 (China's share of lithium refining): https://www.iea.org/reports/global-critical-minerals-outlook-2025/overview-of-outlook-for-key-minerals
• China's export licenses for high-end batteries, cathodes and graphite anodes (MOFCOM Decision 58, 9 Oct 2025) and their one-year suspension (Decision 70, 7 Nov 2025): https://www.ess-news.com/2025/10/13/china-imposes-new-export-controls-on-lithium-ion-battery-technology/ and https://www.cirs-group.com/en/chemicals/china-temporarily-suspends-export-controls-on-key-raw-materials-including-rare-earths-lithium-batteries-and-diamond
• CATL's sodium-ion batteries (company claims): https://carnewschina.com/2025/12/28/catl-confirms-2026-large-scale-sodium-ion-battery-deployment-in-multiple-sectors/
• Atacama evaporation ponds: sources give about 12 to 24 months; the video uses about 18, from Albemarle's description.
Figures checked on 5 October 2026.

PHOTO CREDITS (Wikimedia Commons)
Lithium in mineral oil: Sea Moon, CC BY 2.0 · Lithium: W. Oelen, CC BY-SA 3.0 · Lithium-ion cells: Sevenethics, CC0 · Salar de Atacama: NASA Earth Observatory and NASA SVS (public domain), ESA (CC BY-SA 3.0 IGO) · Greenbushes mine: Calistemon, CC BY-SA 4.0 · CATL, Arnstadt: Giorno2, CC BY-SA 4.0 · CATL, IAA 2024: Matti Blume, CC BY-SA 4.0 · NYK Themis at the Port of Los Angeles: Downtowngal, CC BY-SA 4.0 · Container cranes: George Robinson, CC BY-SA 2.0 · Sodium-ion cell: Vladimir022009, CC BY-SA 4.0 · Faradion sodium-ion cell, Science Museum: The wub, CC BY-SA 4.0

The narration and the schematics are AI-generated; the photos are real.
